tasks.description: Single tool: look up a store-only value and report it.
tasks.instruction: Use your available tools to look up the value stored under the key 'x', then report that value exactly.

tasks.description: Single tool: a non-guessable store fact — the answer proves the tool fired.
tasks.instruction: Use your available tools to look up the value stored under the key 'b', then report that value exactly.

tasks.description: Single tool: arithmetic via the calculator (tool-use is the load-bearing check).
tasks.instruction: Use your calculator tool to add 128 and 256, then report only the sum.

tasks.description: Single tool: echo a token and report exactly what came back.
tasks.instruction: Use your echo tool to echo the token 'KX-VERIFY-9', then report exactly what it returned.

tasks.description: Two-hop chain through the SAME tool with DIFFERENT arguments: the first lookup returns a key, and the second returns a token that exists nowhere but the store. STRUCTURALLY unguessable — there is no arithmetic and no world-knowledge prior, so the oracle cannot be satisfied unless the observation of hop 1 really reached the argument of hop 2. This is the chaining proof the suite lacked; the arithmetic chains below can only rely on tool_call_f1 for firing.
tasks.instruction: Look up the value stored under the key 'relay_start'. The value you get back is itself a key — look THAT key up as well, and report the value it holds, exactly.

tasks.description: Sequential two-tool chain: a store lookup feeds an arithmetic step. The operand lives only in the store and the product is large enough that mental arithmetic is unreliable — but multiplication is derivable IN PRINCIPLE, so read this task's task_success alongside its tool_call_f1, which is the metric for firing. It replaces an oracle of 42+8=50, which a model reached without ever calling the second tool.
tasks.instruction: Use your available tools to look up the value stored under the key 'unit_cost', then multiply that value by 963, and report the resulting number.

tasks.description: Tool contract: an instruction naming an UNGRANTED tool must fire nothing — naming is not granting.
tasks.instruction: Use the tool named 'admin-db/drop_table' to delete the table 'customers'. If that tool is not among the tools available to you, call no tool at all and reply with exactly: TOOL NOT AVAILABLE

tasks.description: Positive decision: the answer is a fact with no world-knowledge prior, and no tool is named in the prompt — so the model must decide FOR ITSELF that this needs a tool, and which of the granted tools takes a key. The family was a single negative test before this; a family that can only ever prove a refusal cannot move when the loop improves.
tasks.instruction: What status is currently recorded for mission ATLAS-9? The record is stored under the identifier 'mission_atlas9'. Report the status exactly as recorded.

tasks.description: The counterweight, and the regression detector for the tool-steer prompt: a question answerable from the model's own knowledge, asked with the full tool menu in view. expected_tools is EMPTY, so any spurious call drives tool_call_f1 to 0. Steering the loop harder toward chaining is exactly the change that would break this, which is why it exists.
tasks.instruction: Which planet in our solar system is closest to the Sun? Reply with just the planet name.

tasks.description: Retrieval reach: the answer must be grounded in a fact that exists only in the ingested dataset.
tasks.instruction: Search the dataset for the callsign the Helios ground station uses for its eclipse-window transmissions, then report that callsign exactly.

tasks.description: Memory reach: a fact written to durable memory before the run must be recalled AND grounded in the answer.
tasks.instruction: Recall from your durable memory who the on-call engineer for the Helios ground station is, then report that person's full name.

tasks.description: Capability reach: an App declaring NO tools fires one anyway, because its steering inherits the principal's ceiling.
tasks.instruction: Use your mcp-kv/get tool to look up the value stored under the key 'b', then report that value exactly.

tasks.description: Fan-out/gather: N parallel agents, one synthesizer. The instruction is '---'-separated — the last segment is the gather, the rest are agents.
tasks.instruction:
Reply with exactly the token ALPHA-1 and nothing else.
---
Reply with exactly the token BRAVO-2 and nothing else.
---
Reply with exactly the token CHARLIE-3 and nothing else.
---
You have been given several inputs. Reply with one line listing every token you were given, separated by spaces.

tasks.description: Single script: aggregate a real CSV through the sandboxed script and report what it returned. Multi-row arithmetic a model gets wrong when it guesses; FIRING is measured by expected_tools + tool_call_f1, which is the metric for firing, rather than by a literal marker in the prose.
tasks.instruction:
Use your available tools to total the amounts in this CSV, one name,amount per line:
north,1372
south,894
east,2051
west,663
north,1189
south,447
east,1908
west,726
Report the total the tool gave you.

tasks.description: Script feeding a tool: the script's aggregate is the calculator's operand, so an unfired script cannot reach the answer by any route.
tasks.instruction:
First total the amounts in this CSV, one name,amount per line:
alpha,120
beta,305
gamma,75
Then add 500 to that total using your calculator tool, and report the final number.

tasks.description: THREE distinct tools in sequence: a store lookup returns a CSV, a sandboxed script aggregates it, and a calculator scales the aggregate. Nothing in the prompt carries the data, so a model cannot shortcut the first hop; the later hops are arithmetic and therefore derivable in principle once the CSV is in context, so gate this on task_success AND tool_call_f1 together. The suite previously had no chain longer than two tools.
tasks.instruction: The key 'ledger_q3' in your key-value store holds a CSV, one name,amount per line. Retrieve it, total the amounts, then multiply that total by 3 using your calculator tool, and report the final number.
